modification_description: Replace the 'actively pursue alternative access routes before considering any purchase' language with a phased, cost-protective three-step rule: (1) first secure essentials with no missed rent, utilities, critical healthcare, or food; (2) then immediately pursue the lowest-risk educational access options such as school/library devices, used/refurbished devices with warranty, or community programs; (3) only consider a purchase if essentials are covered AND a small buffer for surprises is maintained—and even then, prefer used/refurbished over new unless it is the only workable option. This acknowledges that sometimes a quick, low-cost used/refurbished device may be more practical than waiting for programs that may take time.
